mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over 3 consecutive months signals a shift toward monetary easing, lowering discount rates and increasing present-value weights on future cash flows, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% triggers a risk-off reaction, reducing equity risk appetite and compressing forward discount rates, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in rate hike periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs signals a strengthening labor market, prompting higher consumer and business confidence and supporting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in strong employment periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) below -20,000 jobs indicates weakening labor demand, reducing consumer and business confidence and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in weak employment periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) above 113.0 signals robust supply-side expansion, lowering real interest rates and supporting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in strong supply periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) below 110.0 indicates supply-side contraction, raising real interest rates and compressing forward discount rates, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in weak supply periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 210.0 signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to raise rates, which compresses forward discount rates and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in high inflation periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 205.0 signals disinflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to cut rates, which lowers discount rates and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in disinflation periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
